headline: Antique Row weekends, Howard Avenue brick, and why basement trunks sweat in close-in Montgomery
description: Kensington, MD colonials sit on Connecticut Avenue under street trees. why pollen and weekend grit load cool basement ducts.

sections.heading: The basement air handler is storing last April
paragraphs: It cools the colonial. It also sits in the dampest room. Cold trunks sweat. Street-tree pollen is already inside. Together they are what mold needs. A second-floor laundry often sends lint on a long drop to a rear wall.
If wiping the registers only lasts a few days, when you are ready to book, use the [Kensington, MD location page](/locations/kensington).

sections.heading: Typical signs in a Kensington colonial
listItems: Yellow-gray film on upstairs supplies during peak pollen.
Musty basement air when the AC starts after a humid week.
Dust returning fast on Connecticut Avenue or Howard Avenue sides of the house.

sections.heading: Connecticut Avenue is a pollen and grit corridor
paragraphs: Kensington sits between Bethesda and Wheaton: Antique Row on Howard Avenue, Connecticut Avenue through the middle, then Kensington Heights toward Silver Spring. Early- and mid-century colonials have full basements. Those rooms stay cool. Oak and maple on the avenue dump debris onto every stoop. Returns pull it in. Weekend traffic from Antique Row adds a finer grit that a quiet cul-de-sac never sees.
When humid air hits cold supply trunks, that film turns the first AC cycle into a dust event you can see on the registers.
